cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: What Was the Plan?
cards.instruction: Find out what was promised, scheduled, or changed without revealing that you lost track.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. What time did we settle on for Mum's birthday dinner? I'm checking the invitations. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Seven, in the private room. You booked it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Right. How have you written the restaurant name? I want everything consistent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't written anything. You're doing the invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then could you proofread the booking confirmation aloud? I'll type straight from you so we don't introduce any errors.

mechanism: A presents forgotten dinner details as invitation quality control, flattering B into supplying the information while maintaining organizer authority.
confusable: Unlike honest proofreading, A asks basic booking facts A should know and shifts excuses when B exposes the assigned role.
comparison: Family dinner invitations and personal reassurance differ from an outdoor leader accepting a co-leader to recover an itinerary.
seedUse: Use canonical D30-a time/name/confirmation sequence critically, and S02-a changing the official story to maintain cooperation.
